summary: The article accurately describes the RBI's new credit reporting rules, including the effective date, reporting frequency, dispute resolution timeline, and the requirement for lenders to be members of all four credit bureaus.

claims.claim: This change came into effect from July 1, 2026.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the effective date of July 1, 2026, for the RBI's Amended Credit Information Reporting Directions.

claims.claim: Now, they are required to submit this data on four specific dates each month: the 9th, 16th, 23rd, and the last day of the month. A full monthly file is still due by the 5th of the following month.
claims.note: The new reporting schedule mandates data submission on the 9th, 16th, 23rd, and the last day of the month, with a full monthly file by the 5th of the following month.

claims.claim: If you find an error on your credit report, credit bureaus are now mandated to resolve your dispute within 30 days.
claims.note: Credit bureaus are legally obligated to resolve disputes within 30 calendar days.

claims.claim: All regulated lenders must now be members of all four RBI-recognised credit bureaus (TransUnion CIBIL, Experian India, CRIF High Mark, and Equifax India) and share data in a standardised format.
claims.note: All four major credit bureaus (TransUnion CIBIL, Experian, Equifax, and CRIF High Mark) are RBI-licensed, and regulated lenders are required to be members of all of them and submit data in a standardized format.

claims.claim: The RBI's move is part of its ongoing effort, which began in 2024, to make India's credit system more transparent, accurate, and efficient for everyone involved – from borrowers to lenders.
claims.note: The RBI's efforts to enhance credit reporting transparency and efficiency have been ongoing since 2024, with a shift to fortnightly reporting from January 1, 2025, and then to the current weekly reporting.

article_title: Your Credit Score Just Got Faster: RBI's New Weekly Reporting Rules
